order_note: No predecessor: SQL 144 creates one new read function, get_tenant_incoming_transfers(uuid), on the payment transfer, tenant, check sharing and check schema the AWS databases already have (payment_transfers with destination_tenant_id, leg_role, status, environment, check_id and the dates; tenants (id, name); shared_checks (check_id, source_tenant_id, target_tenant_id, revoked_at); check_intake_items and claims for the check context) and the access helpers aws_can_access_tenant(uuid) and is_platform_owner(), with role checksops; a read-only production inspect confirms them. The applying login must be able to reach all five relations as the function's owner past RLS (definer_can_write_relations on each: the table owner without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or a superuser or BYPASSRLS): a DEFINER read filtered by RLS would show the recipient nothing. Expected pre-state in both environments: the function absent (release sql144 v1 / function public.get_tenant_incoming_transfers(uuid): absent). Where it already exists (a re-run) it must be owned by the applying login (functions_owned_by_login), keep its TABLE result (function_results_match) and hold no EXECUTE grant other than checksops and the owner, which the file keeps, and PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role, which it revokes (function_acl_replaceable). The ACL after the apply is checksops and the owner. The API change that exposes the function (aws/functions/api/data.mjs READ_RPCS and RPC_ACCESS_GATES, its own reviewed change) and the website change that reads it tolerate its absence (the RPC fails and the screens show what they show today) and need the guarded Lambda and SPA paths after this pin is applied in that environment; no API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin. Adds no trigger.
